newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B shares end down despite A share gains.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end down despite A share gains.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index closed lower in subdued trading on Tuesday despite modest gains in domestic A shares, brokers said.
The index lost 0.33 point or 0.26 percent to 129.70 on thin turnover of HK$25 million against HK$33 million on Monday.
The A share index finished up 2.69 points or 0.68 percent at 397.15 on turnover of 4.1 billion yuan against 5.0 billion in the previous session.
Foreign investors had abandoned the B share market for more profitable investment targets such as Hong Kong-listed shares, brokers said.
"I am not optimistic about the B share market," a broker at J&A Securities (HK) Co said.
"Foreign investors expect only modest returns from B shares," the J&A broker said.
B share investors were also waiting for listed firms to release their interim results before taking any new positions in the market, brokers said.
None of the 49 Shenzhen-listed B share companies has announced its interim results yet. They have until the end of August.
Brokers said they did not expect any significant improvement in the B share market in the next few months.
A shares were restrained by talk that securities authorities were considering a ban on brokerages using clients' deposits to trade shares, brokers said.
Authorities might let state banks control deposits for stock purchases, they said, adding this would lead to reduced liquidity if the market talk proved true.
"The market cannot bear the implementation of such a policy," said a stock analyst at Hainan Province Trust and Investment Co. "Sentiment is fragile enough."
On the B share market, television tube maker Shenzhen SEG was the heaviest loser, shedding HK$0.20 to HK$5.10 on volume of 41,300 shares.

Bengang Steel remained the market's most actively traded issue, slumping HK$0.03 to HK$2.00 on volume of 2.4 million shares. The stock has held below its offer price of HK$2.38 per share since it made its debut with a listing of 400 million B shares earlier this month.
On the A share market, Shenzhen Development Bank was among the session's most actively traded stock, gaining 0.62 yuan to 34.20 yuan on volume of 6.97 million shares.
